name: House of Elévara
description: US luxury house selling fragrance and leather goods through shop.houseofelevara.com; its Ambassador Program pays commission on every sale through a personal link, starting at 10% and rising to 25% with lifetime sales, and its own program page states there is no cap and no ceiling on earnings.

evidence.summary: The brand's own Ambassador Program page states 'Commission begins at 10% and rises to 25% as you sell. No cap. No expiration.' and, under 'No Cap, No Expiry', 'There is no ceiling on what you earn and no expiration on your link.' The page also shows the earning ceiling as '∞'. This is an explicit no-earnings-cap statement on the brand's own page, so commission_cap is recorded as uncapped.

Program tiers from the same page: Ambassador 10% from the first sale, Signature 15% unlocked at $2,500 lifetime sales, Maison 25% unlocked at $10,000 lifetime sales; tiers never reset. Free to join, no activation fee, no buy-in or inventory; commission is calculated on completed, non-refunded orders and paid monthly. The inaugural collection is led by N° 01 The Parfum ($240 retail), with leather goods arriving in sequence. The contact email admin@houseofelevara.com and phone +1 (307) 289-4953 are published at the foot of the page.

No absolute creator or ambassador count is published on the page checked; the brand is newly launched, but a launch date alone is not low-saturation evidence, so creator_saturation is recorded as unknown.

opportunity.title: House of Elévara Ambassador Program (brand direct)

reasons.niche_fit: Fragrance-led luxury house; the Parfum is the available hero product, with leather goods still arriving, so the promotable catalog is narrow for beauty creators today.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A named Ambassador Program built around personal-link selling, with editorial features for active ambassadors and no following-size requirement.
reasons.compensation: 10% starting rate rising permanently to 15% and 25% at lifetime-sales tiers, with an explicitly uncapped, no-ceiling statement on the brand's own page.
reasons.contact_access: A published contact email and phone number on the program page itself.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free to join with no activation fee, buy-in, minimum purchase or exclusivity.
reasons.credibility: A very new, small house with a short track record and a collection still rolling out.

name: The Detox Market
description: Clean beauty retailer founded in 2010 curating natural and organic skincare, makeup, haircare and wellness brands; its affiliate program runs on Impact and pays 10% per sale on a 30-day cookie.

evidence.summary: LinkClicky's program listing records The Detox Market on the Impact platform at 10% per sale for US and CA regions.
Lasso's listing independently records a 10% per-sale commission and a 30-day cookie duration for The Detox Market affiliate program.
ReferralCandy's beauty affiliate roundup describes The Detox Market as a leading retailer of natural and organic skincare, makeup and wellness products offering affiliates 10% of sales.

A Vendo marketplace write-up says there is 'no cap on the number of referral occurrences' — that is a limit on referral COUNT, not on earnings, so under the directory rules it does not qualify as uncapped and commission_cap is recorded as unknown.

opportunity.title: The Detox Market Affiliate Program (via Impact)

reasons.niche_fit: A broad clean-beauty catalog across skincare, makeup, hair and wellness gives creators a wide range of demo-friendly products.
reasons.ugc_evidence: An established affiliate program on Impact aimed at beauty publishers and creators.
reasons.compensation: 10% per sale with a 30-day cookie, corroborated by multiple listings; no earnings-cap statement was found.
reasons.contact_access: No published program contact email was found on the pages checked; contact runs through Impact.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Impact, subject to merchant approval.
reasons.credibility: Operating since 2010 as a recognized clean-beauty retailer in the US and Canada.

name: Skinsider
description: UK online retailer specializing in Korean skincare, stocking brands such as COSRX, Beauty of Joseon, Mixsoon and Purito; it takes collaboration and affiliate requests through Awin, where approved partners can receive a discount code for their audience.

evidence.summary: Skinsider's own help centre tells creators to send a collaboration request through Awin and links to its affiliate program page at skinsider.co.uk/affiliate-program/, adding that aligned creators can be given a discount code for their audience. The same article publishes the brand's Instagram, Facebook and TikTok profile URLs.

Lasso's listing describes Skinsider's program for vegan and cruelty-free skincare advocates at up to 8% per sale with a 30-day cookie. Because the only published figure is an 'up to' ceiling rather than a confirmed base rate, commission_rate is recorded as null.
No earnings-cap statement and no absolute creator count appears on the pages checked, so commission_cap and creator_saturation are recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: A focused K-beauty catalog (COSRX, Beauty of Joseon, Purito and more) maps directly onto high-demand skincare content.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own help centre routes creators into Awin collaborations with audience discount codes.
reasons.compensation: No confirmed base rate is published; a third-party listing cites up to 8% with a 30-day cookie, so compensation scores conservatively.
reasons.contact_access: A documented help-centre route for collab requests, though no direct program email is published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application and review through Awin; collaboration calls are also announced on the brand's social channels.
reasons.credibility: An established UK K-beauty retailer with a broad branded assortment.

name: Bluemercury
description: US beauty retailer carrying more than 165 skincare, makeup and fragrance brands in stores and online; its affiliate program runs through Rakuten/Linkshare and is free to join, paying commission on recommended products.

evidence.summary: Bluemercury's own help centre confirms it runs a free affiliate program: applicants fill out an application form and email the team, and approved affiliates receive notification from 'our affiliate partner, Rakuten/Linkshare'. The page promotes sharing eligible product links on social channels to earn commission, with a chance to be featured by the brand.

The brand's page describes the commission only as 'competitive' and publishes no rate, earnings-cap statement or creator count, so commission_rate is null and commission_cap and creator_saturation are recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: A 165+ brand assortment across skincare, makeup and fragrance gives creators wide, high-intent product choice.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own help centre actively recruits affiliates to share product links on social channels, with feature opportunities.
reasons.compensation: The rate is not published (described only as competitive), so compensation scores conservatively; no cap statement found.
reasons.contact_access: A documented application route plus a team email contact on the brand's own help page (the address itself was masked in the fetched copy and is therefore not recorded).
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free to join via Rakuten/Linkshare application, subject to approval.
reasons.credibility: A long-established US beauty retailer with a national store footprint.
